chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God be upon him) said: My father said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said:

Verily, Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon him) said: 'O my Lord! I am pleased with what You have decreed: You cause the elderly to die and preserve the young.' Allah, the Mighty and High, replied: 'O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me for being their Sustainer and Provider?' He said: 'Of course, O Lord. You are the best Custodian, and the best Provider.'
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Musa say to God regarding the death of the elderly and the survival of the young?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Prophet Musa (AS) demonstrates *rida* (contentment) with the divine decree of death, specifically noting the contrast between the passing of the elderly and the preservation of the young. Allah responds by affirming His attributes as *Raziq* (Sustainer) and *Kafil* (Guarantor), linking the reality of death to the continuity of divine provision and care. This dialogue underscores the Shia theological emphasis on trusting God’s wisdom in the distribution of life and death, viewing them not as arbitrary but as acts of benevolent guardianship.
